reviews.text: Specializing in caring for our fur babies,  with great kindness and concern.  The doctors and staff are great wonderful.
The staff here is so nice and knowledgeable. They even knew how to work with our behaviorally challenged (aka overly anxious and frightened) dachshund.

We have not had a great experience with this doctor. We have not felt listened to and they diagnosed our dog with a brain tumor and put him on two separate medications. They wanted $4,000 for a dog MRI, this feels criminal and exploitative. When the levels came back for the medication they were at “non-therapeutic levels.” We kept our dog on this medication religiously for about 8 months and noticed no further symptoms. This was strange as a yorkie with a brain tumor would certainly show additional symptoms as we have dealt with this in the past. We decided that we would nitrate the dose down as the bloodwork also should significant liver stress. We have now completely taken our dog off the medication for several months and noticed further issues. This tells us that our dog was misdiagnosed and the vet refused to listen to our concerns about the original diagnosis or what led to the initial seizure. I would certainly not waste the thousands of dollars you will spend here only to receive a dubious diagnosis from a vet who clearly doesn’t want to hear what you have to say and is obviously incorrect. This place will seemingly exploit desperate pet parents. We will happily continue to go elsewhere and would encourage others to do the same. The intellectual arrogance displayed by this “vet” is not worth the prescription pad it’s written on.

A few years ago our dachshund succumbed to the dachshund curse and ruptured a disc, losing his ability to walk. We rushed him here, and the service could not have been better. My rapid-metabolizing pup goes through medication really quickly; therefore, his pain was difficult to control. But the staff was extra diligent with his medication plan to remedy that. I felt so terrible putting my pup through an extensive surgery, but even doctor hugged when when I sobbed while picking up my pup.

Overall, absolutely incredible service that seems to be rarer and rarer these days. I would not hesitate having Vet Neuro take care of my beloved pet again.

Dr Moore took really good care of my dog also Dr Costa was very nice, Ashley the vet tech was absolutely amazing and very thought full, Ashley the receptionist and a gentleman also receptionist  (I’m sorry I don’t remember his name) was very friendly and professional

Our French Bulldog was seen by Dr. Knowles for back pain. We could not have had a better experience. She was wonderful and thorough. I never felt rushed and she took time to go over every single detail. To top it off our dog is not people friendly and she did amazing with him.

Cannot recommend this place enough. The service and care from the front desk staff, techs, and doctors is outstanding. It is expensive, but 100% worth it if you can afford it. Our Corgi had spine surgery to decompress a disk. He was not using his back legs at all before we brought him in, then 2 days later we picked him up and with sling support he walked out with me. Dr. Greatting was phenomenal, she truly saved our pup. His disk was 90% compressed and would not have been able to recover on his own. His entire bill that covered x-rays, MRI, surgery, 2 over night stays, etc. was just over $11k. I truly feel like we got what we paid for even post op, the communication and care has been great. Now our pup will be able to have his quality of life back! Thank you VNC!
The doctors and staff here truly care about your pet. Highly recommend. Worth the 5 hour drive each way for me.

Dr. Stainback and Dr. Lombardo are not only wonderful neurologists, but they are also wonderful people. Our baby, Poppy presented with a very complex case. While only 5 years old, her disease was very serious and took her life. For the 5-6 weeks that Poppy was under the care of VNC, we felt they had our best interests in mind and went above and beyond to treat Poppy. She was even hospitalized for 5+ days during this period. Every day the doctor called us. Yes, you heard that right, the actual doctor, which is basically unheard of in today’s day and age. Dr. Stainback and Dr. Lombardo spent countless hours at visits with us, treating Poppy while she was hospitalized, and on the phone with us during extremely difficult conversations to make sure we were fully informed about her condition, the treatment options, and the pros and cons of every medication, procedure, scan, etc. While Poppy succumbed to her disease, I know wholeheartedly that we did everything we could as her family and that Dr. Stainback and Dr. Lombardo did everything they could as her doctors.

When it came time to say goodbye, both doctors spent considerable time with us. Sharing stories of Poppy from her time at VNC, reassuring us that while saying goodbye feels impossible, we should know in our hearts that we truly gave it our all. I acknowledge that this is the worst part of their job, but it brought some peace on an otherwise terrible day to know that everyone that ever met Poppy saw how happy and loving she was and we really appreciate the time and care Dr. Stainback and Dr. Lombardo gave us.

No one wants to be on a first name basis with a neurologist. No one wants their family member to go through any of this, but knowing we had truly amazing and caring professionals to help us does bring peace.

The entire team at VNC is world-class. While I hope to not need their services in the future, I know I am lucky to have found amazing people that love and care about our animals as much as we do.

I can’t say enough good things about our experience with Vet Neuro. From the moment we walked in, everyone was incredibly kind, compassionate, and personal. The reception staff and technicians made us feel genuinely cared for, and that continued throughout our entire visit.

Dr. Costa and Dr. Plummer were both wonderful. They were professional, knowledgeable, understanding, and incredibly patient with my 14-year-old old man, Tug. They took the time to listen to my concerns, thoroughly evaluate him, and talk through our options without ever making us feel rushed. Most importantly, I felt like they understood that, at this stage of Tug’s life, the goal isn’t simply to pursue every possible intervention—it’s to make thoughtful decisions that give him the best quality of life for whatever time he has left. They helped us come up with a plan that truly feels right for him.

As a veterinarian myself, I know how much goes into providing this level of care, and I was extremely impressed with the entire team. It can also be difficult being on the other side of the exam table with your own pet, especially one who has been with you for so many years. I’m incredibly grateful for the compassion, patience, expertise, and kindness they showed both Tug and me.

Thank you to the entire Vet Neuro team for taking such wonderful care of my old man. It means more to me than you know. ❤️
Kind, intelligent, compassionate staff. Really great at answering questions and helping with medications. Best vet experience I have had.

Me and my dog Apollo absolutely LOVE Dr. Parker. My dog has been diagnosed with and on meds for epilepsy for almost 3 years. It took us a long time to find a knowledgeable, caring and reputable doctor like Dr. Parker and we’re incredibly lucky we did. Not only has Dr. Parker been incredible caring for his epilepsy and treatment, he also goes the extra mile to ensure he is safe for other procedures and treatments. I am highly skeptical about where I take my dog to, he’s my kid and means the world to me. But I can comfortably say Dr. Parker is the ONLY person I would EVER trust with my dogs life. Just wanted to say thank you to the staff at VetNeuro for caring for Apollo these last few years and special thanks to his wonderful doctor. You guys are the best 🐾🤍

Incredibly happy with my experience every step of the way at VNC. When I called to make a neurology appointment for my 11 year old Ranger, I was met with the most helpful and kind guidance. We were able to be seen the same day for an MRI due to Rangers state, and Dr. Oz was informative, patient, and comforting. Thank you for giving us the answers we needed.

Professional,  kind, compassionate,  thorough.
They love your animal as their own. They find the issue and make a game plan to heal, help and give your animal quality of life

As both a breeder and a pet owner, I am incredibly grateful for the care we received from Dr. Knowles, Dr. Lombardo, and the entire team. From the very first phone call through our appointments and follow-up care, everyone treated us with kindness, compassion, and genuine concern.

As breeders, we've worked with a number of veterinarians and specialists over the years, and I can honestly say the level of care we received here was exceptional. Every specialist we interacted with went above and beyond. It never felt like we were just another appointment. Everyone was invested in Bumble's case and genuinely wanted the best possible outcome.

What stood out the most was that Dr. Knowles personally took the time after business hours to call me and go over Bumble's case in detail, answering every question and making sure I understood the plan moving forward. That level of dedication and compassion is something you simply don't see every day.

The communication, professionalism, and genuine love they have for their patients gave me complete confidence that my puppies were receiving the very best care. Thank you for going above and beyond for Bumble and for supporting us every step of the way. We are truly grateful and couldn't recommend your team more highly.

Roxanne
Howlin Hounds

Our little 4.5 lb Yorkie was ran over by our golf cart. Dr. Parker was especially reassuring and took the time to answer all of our questions, helping us feel confident and comfortable with our pet’s care. He recommended an MRI to evaluate his brain as he wasn’t able to walk at the time. Dr Parker evaluated the MRI with us and showed us the brain and spinal swelling he observed. He didn’t think surgery was needed but recommended a neck brace for 2 months. The MRI was a few thousand dollars but we were thankful he didn’t need surgery. Everyone was kind, honest, professional, and genuinely concerned about our pet’s well-being. We are very grateful for the excellent care and highly recommend this office.

It’s every dachsund parent’s worst nightmare… we took Elliot in to his primary care when he stopped wanting to go up his ramp. They identified a sore spot and put him on meds and we monitored him. Four days later on friday evening, he had gone from slightly weak on his back legs to the first signs of dragging his paws. I took him in to the ER and that vet confirmed he was showing signs of neurological issues so i took Elliot home and planned on making an appointment with vet neuro first thing in the morning.

By midnight  his back legs were fully paralyzed; as you can imagine it was the longest morning ever. Fortunately he was able to have imaging and surgery done the same day and Dr. Moore was very communicative throughout the whole process. The staff even called the day after discharge to see how Elliot was doing!

I can’t recommend vet neuro enough; the quality of care and amazing people there shine through in the outstanding results. From the bottom of our hearts, thank you so much.

I cannot thank this clinic and Dr. STAINBACK for all she  did for my baby girl, Poppy. Poppy is doing great . Thank you and your staff for all you did. The staff was so good about calling us to ask how Poppy was doing after surgery. Thank you so much. Nancy Nys

Dr. Lovato was wonderful to work with and did a fantastic job taking care of my chihuahua. He had to have surgery for herniated disc. He's doing so much better now and I'm so grateful for Dr. Lovato's care and everyone at the clinic has been so lovely and compassionate.

This is the best vet's and facility that I have ever been to. Everyone is happy, very experienced and extremely caring. Facility is gorgeous and very clean. Dr Parker did an amazing job fixing my BrunoMarz. I will be referring them to everyone. They take the time to get it right the first time. Thank you so much Dr. Parker and staff. I know that you guys spoiled my baby because everyday for a week or so he kept wanting to go back. He loved you guys.
The amount of dedication and accommodating appointment length made me feel at ease for my dog's... Whatever it was. He is so much better thanks to the keen attention of Dr. Knowles!

I went in support of a friend who's dog was very ill,(My late dog Buster was her boyfriend).
They were very kind and professional. They had her healed up good as new in just a few days thankfully.
Thank you to the staff & animal Dr's

Our French bulldog was regularly seen here for over a year to manage autoimmune encephalitis, and I can’t say enough good things about this clinic. We were so happy with the care she received, and she was able to progress back to normal motor function and stability. When she passed away due to an unrelated cancer, Dr. Lovato sent us the kindest card. It was so nice to hear from the staff who had taken such good care of her and loved her. It meant so much to us. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this clinic to anyone whose pet has a neurological condition.
This vet practice is very well run and very customer service friendly.  Can’t recommend them enough for your pet who may have neurological issues.

It's been almost 8 Months since our dog Nascie was diagnosed with a Brain Tumor that was confirmed by an MRI and NOT ONCE has Dr. Moore returned Any of My calls to speak to him. After several medications mistakes that he has made he will not call me, instead I spend time talking to a CSR there. What happens is after you leave and if you have any issues you go into a phone queue to speak to someone, someone who works from home like Leslie who had a crying baby in the background as I am trying to tell her Nascie had a seizure.  This person than takes down the information and advises "SOMEONE" will call you back within a day or two.  When they call back its never the same person, its another CSR who gives you the doctors Response and if you have a question about the doctors response, than its another "SOMEONE" will call you back.  In our case Dr. Moore made several medication mistakes! First I was told after her diagnosis to wean her off the Prednisone, so I did that and Nascie then start having tearing from her eyes. I had to call and let a CSR know that I weaned her off the Prednisone and I think that was a mistake her eyes are tearing up and she appears to be in discomfort. I had to wait a day for a call back, which was from another CSR to tell me Dr. Moore said the optic nerve doesn't touch the tumor. She is probably having allergies. HOWEVER, I researched this and told the CSR that "Yes, a brain tumor in a dog can put pressure on the optic nerve causing significant eye issues, including tearing, inflammation, and pain" than I had to wait for the CSR to go to Dr. Moore and wait for another call back only for the next CSR to tell me Dr. Moore said to put her back on the Prednisone.   He should have never taken her off the prednisone, from my research the prednisone reduces the swelling around the tumor.  NEXT he told me to wean her off the Levetiracetam that was initially prescribed by our Vet. When I asked why are we weaning her off the Levetiracetam he said because Zonisamide has better results, so I listened to him.  It's important to note that after Nascie started taking the Levetiracetam she didn't have anymore seizures. She had a good 2 weeks of no seizures until the MRI was done and we followed Dr. Moore orders.  Within 3 days of Nascie being weaned off Levetiracetam SHE HAD A SEIZURE ON Sept. 2, another one on Sept 3rd, another one on Sept. 5th and another one on Sept. 6th. Finally they call me back and I asked WHY DID WE WEAN her off the Levetiracetam if it was working? The CSR told me because most people can't stick to the strict every 8 hour Schedule.  I was never told this! No ONE ASKED ME and I WAS NOT WORKING so this should have been asked of me not assumed!  Next was in October Dr. Moore said I was not given the correct dosage of Levetiracetam. I advised I was giving Nascie what her VET who initially prescribed it told me to give her.  Dr. Moore's CSR told me it should be 250MG 3 times a day. We were giving her 125MG 3 times a day. It's important to note From the time we put her back on the Levetriacetam in early Sept until October, Nascie had no issues!  However, I increased the dose per what Dr. Moore told his CSR to tell me and within 3 days my 15 pound dog was vomiting, had diarrehea and couldn't stand on her own without falling over.  I than researched what happens when you give a dog too much Anti Seizure medication, I mean my little 15 pound dog was getting 850 mg combined (250mg 3x a day of Levetiracetam and 50mg twice a day of Zonismide) and everything Nascie was going through is what happens when you over medicate a dog.  I stopped Immediately and within a week she was better, but it took 2 weeks for the diarrehea to clear up.  And in the following months anytime I had a question or asked to speak to Dr. Moore he will not call me.  Now, 8 months later she's having Seizures and I've asked for someone else other than Dr. Moore. Nascie initially saw Dr. Knowels when she was 2 years old. I was told I would get a call back, that was 5 days ago! SHAME ON ALL OF THEM! She's Important. She MATTERS!

Dr. Lovato and Dr. Lombardo saved Maisy's life. Maisy is my best friend, my teaching assistant, my agility and sport partner, and my soul dog in all aspects of both of our lives. On March 11th she developed an acute case of cervical IVDD - a disc expulsion effecting her C4/5 vertebrae along with spinal cord bruising. Of course we didn't find this out until the following day. On March 11th Maisy went from stifly walking around and running in the yard to completely paralyzed from the head down. All within 4 hours. We luckily had gone to the vet that morning when I realized she wasn't feeling herself, so we were able to get into Neuro the next day. While she stayed over night in the ER, she developed respiratory distress and was deemed to have a very poor prognosis and would most likely not survive the transfer from the ER to neuro. But she did! We transfered there with oxygen and upon arrival she was taken straight for an MRI and then straight to surgery after that. This team was beyond amazing from every interaction, and I know my best friend would likely not be alive or suffering from a terrible quality of life without them. Thank you so much for you care, compassion, knowledge and skill to make these miracles happen.

Within 24 hours of our Frenchie suddenly losing the ability to use her rear legs we found both comfort and answers with Dr. Lombardo and her entire team. They took amazing care of Basil, and have checked in to make sure she is still improving. Fortunately we did not need to proceed with surgery but I would have had no qualms about trusting my pups care to this clinic. They are wonderful.

We saw Dr. Nathan Bernier-Parker who exceeded our expectations. He was sure to sit down and take ample time with us to assure we understood everything going on with our pup Taubi (pituitary tumor), went over the MRI in great detail and got us going in the right direction.
Garbage service & unconscious people

This team has created a truly memorable and unique place for one of the most traumatic experiences a pet owner can go through. Our pup was rushed for an emergency visit, was in surgery 3 hours later, and walking again in 2 days. I know this cannot be the same outcome for all pups but we loved the team that helped us and Dr Parker was incredible! Thank you VNC!

I recently had the luck of being assigned Dr. Jennifer Balaban for my dog’s back pain.  Prior to the appointment I spoke to the front desk staff numerous times for updates on medications given etc and they were always professional and courteous in explaining what would happen at my appointment and what I needed to do if an emergency occurred prior to the appt.
On the day of the appt, we arrived with all the other 10 o’clock patients and immediately were placed in a room.  Dr. Balaban immediately impressed me by starting the conversation with her review of the X-rays and lab work sent over by my regular Vet. She had already researched the data and provided me the information she felt was most likely going to be the issue. She examined my dog with kindness and empathy to her pain while explaining next steps. She also succinctly described what was happening with my dog in words I could understand!
We followed all of Dr. Balaban’s advice on additional tests and at the end of the day we were so pleased to know that her initial thoughts on what was wrong were correct because it was treatable and fixable.  Dr. Balaban is all business (which I appreciate!) and quickly determined how to handle this situation. She was amazing and I would recommend her and this facility to anyone with neuro needs.  I am sure this was a routine exam/situation for her but for us it was the most important thing in our world and she made sure we knew we were in good hands.  Thank you Dr. Balaban and staff!

Considering this is THE only neurology specialty center in AZ for your dog .. I took my dog here for severe encephalitis. She died while on treatment. I called the clinic and left a VM canceling our appointment which was scheduled the very day after she died. The clinic never called back to give their condolences or discuss anything. Considering they have “patient care coordinators” or whatever I thought that was pretty remiss. I also spent about 7k here in one visit. But I guess they already collected their money.
We never had a definitive diagnosis despite a mired of tests. My dog went into liver failure while on prednisone and fluconazole, a low but definite risk. We were never told to have screening labs. Our follow up appointment was pushed back from 2 week follow up to 3.5 weeks due to the Christmas and new years holiday. Could my dogs death have been prevented..? Maybe only in the short term But I sure as heck would have done anything to try. The lack of close follow up, guidance and lack of care for the patient once they have passed is unacceptable.
I felt like I was in great care at my initial consult but that’s where it ended.

We were referred to Dr. Lydia Lovato for our kitty who had a mystery illness. During our time working with Dr. Lovato, she was very caring with our kitty and made sure that she was always comfortable. She always made an effort to explain why she was ordering tests and what she was looking for during each visit. Despite many tests and medications, our kitty got worse and we unfortunately had to put her down. Even though this experience was awful and traumatic, Dr. Lovato made sure to personally walk us through it and was so kind during the entire time. All of the staff were so helpful during that time as well. Even though we never found a diagnosis for our kitty, I know that Dr. Lovato and the staff at VNC did everything they could to help her. My wife and I are eternally grateful to them for everything they did for our kitty and for us. We hope to never have to see them again, but if we need a neurologist for another kitty, we will certainly come back.

We saw Dr. Knowles today for my dog Bonnie, and I truly can’t say enough good things about our experience. Dr. Knowles was incredible and very knowledgeable, compassionate, and so patient. She took the time to explain everything clearly and made sure Bonnie was comfortable every step of the way. The entire staff was AMAZING and treated us with such kindness and care. It’s obvious they genuinely love what they do. I’m so grateful we found Dr. Knowles (recommended by my mom) and her team, and I highly recommend them to anyone needing exceptional care for their pet. Everyone was so patient with us and answer ALL my questions.

IM SO THANKFUL TO EVERYONE.

I got a call from Niko he was so good at explaining my wants and needs from  gracies blood work he explained everything in detail I was so nervous about hearing this I was scared it was going to be bad.. and Niko was amazing and patient, I kept overtalking him.and still he was very calm and undeststanding, thank you niko..

I cannot say enough good things about Veterinary Neurological Center. From our very first visit through surgery and recovery, every single person we interacted with was kind, patient, thorough, and incredibly supportive.

The entire staff took the time to explain each step of the process and answered all of our questions without ever making us feel rushed or dismissed. When you’re facing something as overwhelming as neurological surgery for your dog, that level of care and communication means everything.

Dr. Knowles was absolutely amazing. She met with us at every appointment, explained Ivy’s condition in a way we could truly understand, and showed genuine compassion for both Ivy and us as owners. Her knowledge, patience, and calm confidence gave us so much peace during a very stressful time.

If my memory serves correctly, Dr. Moore was the surgeon, and we are incredibly grateful for the skill and care that went into Ivy’s procedure. Knowing she was in such capable hands gave us so much reassurance.

Our dog Ivy is a 10-year-old dachshund, and deciding to move forward with surgery was not an easy decision - emotionally or financially. All in, we spent about $10,000, so it was a significant investment for us. That said, it was worth every single penny. We never felt pressured, only supported and fully informed so we could make the best decision for her.

Ivy was diagnosed with IVDD, with a significant herniated disc in her lower neck (C7–T1). After months of pain, stiffness, and weakness that continued to return despite medication, her condition worsened. At her worst, she could barely walk and was dragging her left back leg, which was terrifying to watch.

Now, about three months post-surgery, she is like a new dog. She is happier, more comfortable, moving better, and clearly enjoying life again. Seeing her pain-free makes every hard decision worth it.

If you are scared or unsure about next steps for your pet, I truly hope this helps. Choosing Veterinary Neurological Center was one of the best decisions we’ve ever made for Ivy, and we will always be grateful for the compassion, expertise, and care this team provided.
Extremely knowledgeable and caring staff. Got our pup in quickly and follow up regularly. It's hard to find a good specialist close.
The whole team was absolutely amazing and helping me every single time I called, had an appointment, etc. We saw Dr.Oz who was absolutely patient and kind and so helpful with evey step we needed  💙 …
Our pup Bella saw them for a consult. They did a great job! We will be going back to visit them in the future if we need to. We traveled from Colorado. Very friendly and professional staff!
Dr. Parker was absolutely wonderful! Very kind and knowledgeable. My dog is now 3 weeks post op and doing better than ever! He is an 8 year old dachshund with IVDD. Definitely worth it! 10/10

Dr Knowles & the front desk staff are amazing. The kindness, attention to detail but most Dr Knowles is present, attentive & compassionate. We have a surgery planned on Monday & looking forward to our pup healing journey with this team. If you find yourself needing to be here, you’re in good hands. And can I just say what an amazing cute touch! Look at this personal touch on the medicine bag 😍

Dr. Adi Oz is truly the best vet I have ever come across in my life. She is the most compassionate and caring and thoroughly explained my dog’s condition and gave all treatments options and possible outcomes. She truly cares about her patients and does everything she can for them. You can tell she is passionate about what she does and gives it her all to help your dog. She was so good with my Archie who was in so much pain. I can’t thank her enough and highly recommend this place.

If your dog is more than just a pet, don't bring them here. Yes, the times I brought her in and to pick up her medication, they seemed helpful and sweet, but when it mattered, my dog did not matter.

On my dog's last day, the emergency veterinarian seemed shocked that my dog both had a lung tumor and brain tumor and the neurologist said they were not connected. The vet did an ultrasound and found that my dog had lesions that were likely tumors all over her body.

Not only that, but on her last day, I called this group to review her symptoms after 3 seizures. I explained that I was being pressured to put her down in the emergency department, she couldn't stand on her own and I didn't know how much time to give her. The person on the phone, who I think was the same person in another call a couple months back(extremely unhelpful that day), was on the phone (again). They came back hours later with "the vet said, try the steroid twice a day, blah blah blah." I had to literally shout at her because she didn't seem to understand or care (again) that this wasn't that type of conversation or situation.

I ended up putting my best girl down that day, without knowing fully if she would have had more time and not knowing how much more time to give her.

I called after my sweet girl had passed and let a manager know that this person was quite frankly, not smart, helpful or kind. I let them know that I had lived everyday (and still do) wondering if I had the proper support, would I have had more time. The manager then called me back and  told me she ran the situation by a vet and I did the "right" thing- but this wasn't exactly the issue and the manager seemed to deflect this.
There is nothing that could be done so I declined to waste more time.

I regret whole heartedly spending time and money with this group, it's time I will never get back and my family I will always wonder about. Please, be very careful if you decide to work with this group.

This is my second time seeking their help and expertise. Teddy came to the center a Stage 4 IVDD paralyzed in his back legs.  Dr Moore and Dr Lombardo along with a great staff took care of our sweet boy.  Now 10 days out from surgery Teddy is walking, slowly but walking.  Thank you all so much.

Dr. Plummer and the staff here were incredible. Our cat Obi was very sick and they gave us the best possible care and helped us through the grief of having to say goodbye to him. Dr. Plummer was informative, thorough, kind and we will be forever grateful for his professionalism and care during such a difficult time.

If I could give this place 10 stars I would!!

*The picture is Kiko immediately after I picked her up and she was her happy normal self!

I am SO happy and pleased with my visit at VetNeuro. My pup Kiko, small female Pekingese, was referred to them from Dr. Savard over at Raintree (also excellent vet by the way), for possible seizures. Of course, as a pet owner, this is scary and daunting. Your best friend could potentially be sick and you aren't sure why... First of all, it was so easy to contact and call VetNeuro's front desk, they always answered the phones promptly and kindly and were so informative. Kiko is usually very scared, timid, and shaking whenever she enters a veterinary clinic, but she was so curious and not scared when we initially walked in. She only was a little anxious when they took her from me to do the testing, but that is pretty normal. Compared to all her other vet visits, Kiko was so much more relaxed and I know it is due to the comfortable and welcoming environment that VetNeuro creates, from the people to the waiting room to the patient room. It didn't have that "sterile" hospital-type of feeling and I know Kiko could sense that. Keep in mind Kiko is a highly anxious dog that is scared of people due to a previous owner abusing her.

I had a ton of questions, naturally as a worried dog mom, and asked things like what can we do, what is the cause, what does an MRI do, how does that happen exactly, etc. I just wanted to be informed because it helped calm my nerves. Also, I have some trauma from my first dog dying from sickness and the vet was extremely cold and insensitive, so I was just a little scared myself.

But Dr. Laura Browand-Stainback was amazing. She was kind, and the genuine kind of nice! I felt like she listened to all of my questions and answered them, she didn't feel like she was rushing to head to the next patient either. She even came back to the room because I had more questions, which I really appreciated. I opted in for the MRI and they provided me with a fully itemized estimated quote beforehand so I could financially prepare myself.

They called me as Kiko was put under anesthesia successfully and then gave me a call when she started to wake up. Her test results came back pretty normal with diagnosed genetic epilepsy, but thankfully nothing worse or scarier than that. Again, Dr. Laura explained everything to me and I felt comfortable. And the most telling part was, Kiko came back prancing into the room her normal happy self as well. Even when we left the clinic and got home, she was eating and playing completely normal and happy!

As a young dog mom/owner, taking your pup to the vet can be daunting and scary, anxiety-wise but also financially (we had no dog insurance). I felt very comfortable with all of the staff, front desk, assistants, and Dr. Laura. And because I was informed of everything and because they happily answered all of my questions, I felt like the few thousand dollars for the MRI test were completely justified and I was more than happy to spend that on my little pup.

I have never had such a pleasant experience with a Vet before, let alone a Vet Neurology clinic.

I will be giving Kiko her anti-convulsant medication moving forward, monitor her, and hope she does not have another seizure episode.

Thank you so much VetNeuro, I highly recommend you!!!!

- Allison
We use them for our OFA BAER Hearing testing on litters! Great staff and very quick and professional!

The team at VNC is simply the best. They are thoughtful and attentive and never more than a phone call away.

My boy was diagnosed with IVDD and needed to have surgery. Dr. Knowles and Dr. Stainback took amazing care of him and assured my anxieties along the way. They have been patient with my seemingly endless questions and have been nothing but amazing to my dog.

In all, surgery, diagnostics, aftercare, and medication was a little over $10k for a miniature dachshund. It’s never a happy time to visit VNC, but I owe them so much for bringing Lincoln back to his former self.

We are incredibly grateful to Dr. Knowles and the entire team at the Veterinary Neurological Center. When our dog suddenly became paralyzed in her hind legs due to IVDD, we were devastated. Dr. Knowles was compassionate, honest, and thorough—she explained that a successful outcome would depend on many factors aligning, starting with the MRI. Thankfully, everything went well, and our dog was taken into surgery immediately.

Today, exactly two years later, she’s not only walking—she’s running, jumping, and enthusiastically chasing squirrels. We can’t thank Dr. Knowles enough for her expertise and care during such a critical time.

My dog has been having seizures for quite some time and medication prescribed by general vet weren’t working so we were referred to this facility.  Clean office and nice staff.  I appreciated the honesty of the vet and resident vet and didn’t feel like they jammed unnecessary treatment recommendations down my throat like some places do.  Reasonably priced services as well.
Great staff and Veterinarians.

I had a really great experience with this practice.

It was a stressful process initially coming to Vet Neuro Center for an MRI due to IVDD pain for my cavalier. She ended up needing surgery after reviewing the MRI due to long-standing and acute injury to her disc.

Our vet, Dr Lovato -- was so caring and explained everything wonderfully. Due to schedules, I had to end up scheduling with Locum Neurologist Dr Greatting since Dr Lovato was on vacation the week we needed to have the surgery. I was so nervous about my dog's surgery but both doctors walked me through everything and were very communicative throughout the process.

Everyone at the front desk is also so kind, pleasant, and helpful. They also helped work with my insurance company Trupanion to get pre-approval for everything. My dog LOVED coming here to see all the friendly techs. Two weeks post op and my dog is recovering nicely. This was definitely one of the best vet clinic experiences I've ever had.
Dr Knowles was thorough and cost aware as my fur baby is almost 11 years old. She was compassionate and I would highly recommend to anyone who needs a neuro consult on your pet.

I'll tell you first hand that going to a neurologist with your beloved pet is never a lovely experience to start with. It's so emotional, scary and just plain rotten to be going thru. This clinic so far (only one visit, going for follow up appt soon) is great.  We had a small issue come up and they handled it well and just made sure I was comfortable with the care & treatment of my Frenchie. He's not even 6½ and unfortunately this is his second neurological incident and MRI. The team was so so nice.  Front office staff has been following up on how he's doing. My resident neurologist also followed up personally to see how he was doing. I def feel that they genuinely care. This place is over 2hrs away from me and was worth the drive. They're the closest animal neurologist to me since moving to AZ in May. I was really hoping moving away from our other neurologist wouldn't be a big deal... was hoping my pup wouldn't need one again. I'm hoping that my second visit goes well and that I don't need to adjust my 5 star rating. This place has been a class act.  Even got a hug from the doctor since I was a sappy mess with all of the information and procedures that were required.

Do not go here if you want to pick your dog up alive. In November of 2024 I paid thousands of dollars for my beautiful Blueberry to fix a herniated disc. While he was under their supervision, after surgery, they took him to go potty and lost him. He was found on the highway; DOA. He wasn’t even 5 years old.

I'm a 100% disabled Veteran, Blueberry was my lifeline. I haven't left my house since except to go to therapy. This is the most horrific thing I've ever endured, and I have been through a heck of a lot. I will never forgive myself for trusting them to take care of my sweet baby.

Feel free to message me if you need a referral to another vet.

I feel they really care. Dr.Knowles instincts and thought process towards my dogs epilepsy feels sincere and responsible. I appreciate the consistent communication/updates that we receive after reporting any of his seizures online. (Which is also very convenient) Front desk is always super sweet and professional. I feel that my little boy is well taken care of by them and I am super grateful for their help aiding to his epilepsy.

This place saved my dog's life!!
My dog has received wonderful care at VNC! Dr. Parker is who we usually sees and he is so knowledgable and kind. My dog could barely walk and was diagnosed with meningitis when we first visited. He's now well on his way to a full recovery thanks to the doctors and techs here.
The customer service is also amazing. Anytime I call with a question or concern I always get a quick response.

Thank you so much VNC!
Very caring staff that knows what they’re doing. I feel very fortunate to have you guys as a resource and thank you from Alex and I (and Oso).

Dr Knowles and the entire staff have been wonderful to Lolli and ourselves. They treated her for a neck/spinal cord injury for over 10 years. The treatment went beyond just regular office visits. Their communication with Lolli’s regular vet was outstanding.  She was not expected to live past seven or eight but instead lived to be almost 13 years old because of their care and concern. We appreciate everything they did right up till the end to make her life full of joy and happiness. She added so many blessings to our lives.   We would highly recommend them to care for any pet that has special needs beyond what an ordinary vet might be able to treat.

Thank you very much for the compassion you had for our dog on his first and only visit while on this Earth. We couldn't have asked for anything more from a staff during the time while there. We are truly grateful, thank you. Rest in peace my love, Chato!
Worth every penny, saved my dogs life.
